title: Put a deadline on a gRPC call
summary: Add a deadline with context.WithTimeout, detect the timeout with status.Code because errors.Is misses it, and pass ctx down to the database on the server.

turns.user: checkout api sometimes just never returns. seems to be when inventory is struggling. hangs until the LB cuts it at 60s

assistant.body: Understood. A gRPC call has no deadline by default. If the ctx you pass has none, it waits until the server answers, and the ctx of an HTTP request has none either. Let's put a 2 second deadline on the call with context.WithTimeout. The deadline also reaches the server, in the grpc-timeout header. While we are here, a timeout becomes ErrInventoryTimeout and the out of stock FailedPrecondition becomes ErrOutOfStock, so the handler can answer 504 and 409.

turns.user: returns in 2s now. but on timeout its 500 not 504. doesnt look like its becoming ErrInventoryTimeout

assistant.body: I checked again, and that was my mistake. grpc-go does not return context.DeadlineExceeded as is. It builds a new status error carrying codes.DeadlineExceeded, and errors.Is does not match that error against context.DeadlineExceeded. Check it with status.Code, the same way as FailedPrecondition.

turns.user: 504 now. also in the inventory logs the UPDATE keeps running to the end after checkout has timed out. some rows have stock taken but the reservation counted as failed

assistant.body: The server ctx already carries the deadline the client set. But Reserve passes context.Background() to ExecContext. In other words, the deadline is dropped at the server's front door and never reaches the database. Pass the incoming ctx downstream.

Note: this only stops a query that is still running after the deadline. If the UPDATE finishes just before the deadline and only the response is late, the stock stays reduced. Closing that gap needs a reservation ID so that Reserve is idempotent.
